tools_setup.none: No supported local AI was available. Nothing was installed or started.
tools_setup.secret.note: Use an existing MCP server. No software is installed. Do not put secrets in names, URLs or arguments. Bearer credentials are held only for this application session.
tools_setup.name: Name

wizard.welcome: Choose your AI, then add external tools only if you want them.
wizard.heading.tools: Choose which tools this connection may use
wizard.ai.intro: ChromaNeural can use its built-in local AI or an Ollama model already available on this computer.
wizard.ai.help: Select an AI found on this computer, then choose Use this AI. Testing asks permission before sending a harmless prompt. If Ollama is missing, open your installed Ollama application and scan again. Nothing is installed, started or downloaded here. If the built-in AI is available, you can use it without Ollama.
wizard.ai.no_ollama: Ollama was not detected. You can continue with the built-in local AI when it is listed. This scan cannot distinguish an absent Ollama installation from one that is not running.
wizard.ai.tools: External tool use requires a selected Ollama model with structured tool support. The built-in AI works independently without external tools. You can still prepare a connection and leave it disabled.
wizard.ai.scan.done: Local AI scan completed. Choose a listed AI; nothing was selected automatically.
wizard.ai.choose: Select a detected AI first. No provider was changed.
wizard.ai.selected: Your AI selection has been saved.
wizard.ai.test.ok: Selected AI returned a response successfully.
wizard.optional.intro: ChromaNeural works without external tools. You can optionally connect an MCP-compatible service or application and approve only the tools you want your selected AI to use.
wizard.management.note: Existing connections stay unchanged. Expert custom configuration and ongoing management are available separately below.
wizard.catalog.intro: Choose what you want to work with. All profiles start disabled. A listed integration is not a compatibility certification: check its status and setup requirements.
wizard.realtime: MCP is for approved information and high-level workflows, never a real-time machine safety or motion-control loop. Safety and control remain with the robot, PLC or device controller. Remote execution remains disabled.
wizard.profile.unavailable: EXPERIMENTAL — NOT AVAILABLE in guided setup yet. No verified compatible launch/connection profile is provided. Nothing will be installed or connected. You can go back and skip external tools.
wizard.profile.unverified: NOT VERIFIED — vendor acceptance with ChromaNeural is not yet complete.
wizard.tooling.detected: Related tooling was found on PATH. This does not establish an available MCP server.
wizard.tooling.absent: No related supported program was found on PATH. No disk or network scan was performed.
wizard.name: Connection name
wizard.name.hint: Required: choose a recognizable name, up to 80 characters. No secrets.
wizard.address.hint: Paste the MCP address supplied by this integration, usually beginning with https://. An ordinary website or broker address is not enough. Address checks do not contact the service.
wizard.token.hint: Only if your service requires it. Stored in this application session only; never saved in configuration. Leave blank when no token is required.
wizard.token.help: Open the service's MCP, API, Developer or Integrations settings. Follow its instructions for an access token with the least necessary permissions. Never paste a password or browser cookie. Browser sign-in/OAuth is not implemented here; ask the service administrator for a supported access-token connection. Tokens are sent only to the exact approved HTTPS address.
wizard.clipboard.empty: The clipboard has no text to paste.
wizard.local.hint: Choose the installed MCP program for this profile. Finding a file does not verify its publisher or grant permission to start it.
wizard.local.help: Use the program identified in this profile's integration documentation. On Windows it is normally an .exe file. Choose application lets you select it yourself. Only a known program name on PATH and your existing ChromaNeural configurations are checked automatically; files are never run during discovery.
wizard.local.none: No compatible MCP application was detected automatically.
wizard.arguments.hint: Optional launch arguments: add one item per argument exactly as the integration documentation specifies. Do not enter passwords or tokens here. They would be saved in configuration.
wizard.valid: ✓ Values look valid. No connection has been made.
wizard.review.intro: You are about to approve this exact connection:
wizard.review.no_tools: Testing contacts the service or starts the selected local program. Testing does not approve any tools. The connection stays disabled until you explicitly enable it at the end.
wizard.limits: Existing limits: connection request 10 seconds; discovery worker 20 seconds; tool result 32 KiB; one tool call at a time per task; at most four calls per task. No background polling, fleet discovery or automatic synchronization. The worker suppresses service error bodies to protect secrets, so authentication/TLS/server errors may require checking the service locally.
wizard.connection.ok: ✓ Connection successful. Choose tools to approve next.
wizard.tools.intro: Nothing is selected automatically. Select only individual tools you understand and want your AI to use. Observation is the default selection mode.
wizard.tools.untrusted: Names, descriptions and read-only hints come from the server and are untrusted data. They are not safety guarantees. Enforce read-only permissions on the service itself where available.
wizard.tools.none: No MCP tools were returned. You can finish with the connection disabled, or go back and check the service configuration.
wizard.tools.changes: Allow selection of other / potentially state-changing tools
wizard.tools.risk: These tools may change devices, configuration, files or external services. This is separate permission to select them, not approval to execute. Never approve safety-critical motion or machine-control tools here. You must still approve each selected tool afterwards. Allow selection?
wizard.tools.no_description: No description supplied by the service.
wizard.tools.unknown: Not listed as an observation tool in this profile; separate consent required.
wizard.finish.security: Only this approved target and your selected tools receive permission from this setup. Access tokens are not permanently stored. Tool results remain untrusted data. Remote execution remains disabled.
wizard.finish.enable: Enable this connection when I finish
wizard.finish.skipped: External tools skipped. Your local AI setup is complete.
wizard.finish.existing: Currently enabled saved connections: {count}. Existing connections are not changed by skipping. Manage them under Advanced / Developer.
wizard.error.config: The settings could not be saved or are invalid. Check the displayed values. No fallback was selected.
wizard.error.operation: This operation could not be completed. Check the configuration and try again; nothing was enabled automatically.
wizard.error.timeout: The connection timed out. Check that the service is running, then try again.
wizard.error.ai.discovery: Local AI discovery could not finish. Scan again; no provider was changed.
wizard.error.ai.test: The selected AI did not return a usable response. Check that it is available and its model is installed. No fallback was used.
wizard.error.address: Enter the integration's valid HTTPS address without credentials, query parameters or a fragment. HTTP is allowed only for an explicit loopback address. The address must lead to an MCP service.
wizard.error.program: Choose an existing local program using its full path. Shells and package installers are not allowed. Check any advanced arguments against the tool documentation.
wizard.error.name: Enter a connection name of 1–80 characters without control characters.
wizard.error.token: The access token is invalid or the address is not HTTPS. Paste only the token supplied by this service, without spaces or line breaks.
wizard.error.changed: The saved target or permissions changed. Go back and approve/test the connection again.
wizard.error.approval: Required provider or tool approval is missing. Nothing was enabled.
wizard.error.remote: The service could not be reached or did not accept the connection. Check its address, access token and service status. Go Back to edit, or choose Approve connection and test to retry. Authentication/TLS details are intentionally not exposed here.
wizard.error.local: The local application could not start or did not complete MCP discovery. Check the selected program and its setup requirements. Go Back to edit, or choose Approve connection and test to retry.
wizard.profile.opcua.name: Industrial Equipment — OPC UA
wizard.profile.opcua.description: Observe industrial information through the OPC Foundation MCP server. Machine control is not certified by this profile.
wizard.profile.opcua.help: Install/configure the official OPC Foundation opcua-mcp tool yourself first. Find compatible applications checks that exact program name on PATH; otherwise choose the installed program. Review the vendor certificate/trust setup separately. ChromaNeural starts a fresh local server per operation: workflows requiring a persistent OPC UA session are NOT VERIFIED. No machine writes are approved by default.
wizard.profile.ros2.name: Robotics — ROS 2
wizard.profile.ros2.description: Robotics telemetry and diagnostics are the intended scope; no robot motion is enabled.
wizard.profile.ros2.help: ROS 2 alone is not an MCP server. The ROS community has published adapters, but an official, bounded ChromaNeural robotics profile has not been verified. Only the ros2 program on PATH is checked as a tooling hint. No ROS graph discovery or robot connection is attempted.
wizard.profile.isaac.name: Simulation & Digital Twin — NVIDIA Isaac Sim
wizard.profile.isaac.description: Search Isaac Sim developer knowledge through NVIDIA's documented MCP service; this does not control a simulation.
wizard.profile.isaac.help: An administrator must first deploy NVIDIA's Isaac Sim MCP knowledge server and configure its required NVIDIA credentials outside ChromaNeural. Ask for its exact MCP service address. The documented service uses /mcp. Paste the supplied address; a local service may use an explicit 127.0.0.1 address. No container is installed or started here, and finding Isaac Sim itself would not prove this separate service is ready.
wizard.profile.emqx.name: IoT & Device Fleets — MQTT / EMQX
wizard.profile.emqx.description: Device and telemetry infrastructure; no broker subscriptions, publishing or fleet discovery occur here.
wizard.profile.emqx.help: A broker address is not an MCP service address. EMQX documents MCP over MQTT, which this client does not implement, plus adapters with separate broker credentials. A compatible bounded adapter and credential route must be verified before this profile can connect. No broker password is requested or saved here.
wizard.profile.homeassistant.name: Smart Devices — Home Assistant
wizard.profile.homeassistant.description: Inspect approved home/device information. Device changes require separate tool approval.
wizard.profile.homeassistant.help: Enable Home Assistant's official Model Context Protocol Server integration in Settings → Devices & services. Copy its MCP server address from Settings → System → AI where available, or obtain it from your administrator. Restrict exposed entities/APIs in Home Assistant. This client accepts an administrator-supplied bearer access token over HTTPS; it cannot perform the documented browser OAuth login. If your installation requires OAuth only, stop here. Do not paste a general Home Assistant webpage address.
wizard.profile.siemens.name: Industrial Engineering — Siemens Xcelerator
wizard.profile.siemens.description: Search the official Developer Portal for product and API documentation. No PLC or engineering project control.
wizard.profile.siemens.help: The official Siemens Xcelerator Developer Portal MCP address is already filled in. Review it before approving the connection. The documented askDeveloperPortal tool searches documentation, products and APIs; it does not grant access to your industrial equipment. No local installation is required for this hosted service.
wizard.profile.arduino.name: Embedded Development — Arduino
wizard.profile.arduino.description: Embedded development integration is experimental. No firmware upload or device changes are enabled.
wizard.profile.arduino.help: Arduino documents MCP in App Lab/App CLI Agentic Mode, but that is not proof that an installed arduino-cli program is a compatible standalone MCP server. This profile only checks for arduino-cli on PATH. A reviewed external-client connection and safe tool set are still required. Do not substitute a community firmware-control server automatically.

wizard.profile.rea.name: Developer Analysis — REA
wizard.profile.rea.description: Analyze binaries, applications, firmware and runtime behavior with evidence-backed local reverse engineering.
wizard.profile.rea.hint: REA is an optional local software-analysis tool for developers. ChromaNeural looks only at its own saved connections and REA launchers on PATH. Detection does not verify the integration or approve any tools.
wizard.profile.rea.help: Get REA from https://github.com/morluto/rea or https://rea.tools/. You need an installed rea-agents package and Node.js ^22.19.0, ^24.11.0 or >=26.0.0, plus npm for installation. The official manual installation is npm install --global rea-agents. Review and run it yourself; ChromaNeural does not install anything. Scan again afterward, or choose the installed rea / rea-agents launcher or its scripts/rea.mjs file. ChromaNeural launches that installed script with Node.js and the official mcp argument, without a shell or download. The upstream npx rea-agents setup command can change other agent clients’ configuration: review those changes before approving; it is not required for ChromaNeural. Linux static JavaScript analysis also requires a procps-compatible ps. Tool availability depends on REA and your chosen task. Only the audited REA 6.5.0 static tool subset is verified on Linux with systemd user/cgroup v2 enforcement. Limits: 1.5 GiB memory, one CPU, 64 tasks, 30 seconds per process tree. Other REA versions require a new review.
wizard.rea.detected: REA detected — Version: {version}. Verified profile: REA 6.5.0 on Linux with secure resource isolation.
wizard.rea.absent: REA was not detected on this computer.
wizard.rea.node.missing: ! Compatible Node.js not detected — {version}. See Setup help for required versions.
wizard.rea.npm.missing: npm was not detected. It is needed to install REA; an existing complete REA installation can still be checked.
wizard.rea.optional_engines: Some advanced REA analysis tasks require additional analysis tools. REA will report what is needed for the selected task.
wizard.rea.authorized: Use REA only on software, devices and data you are authorized to analyze.
wizard.rea.untrusted: Analysis results are untrusted data, never instructions to execute. Process execution, device changes and other side effects need separate explicit approval. No tools are approved automatically.
wizard.rea.invalid: Choose an installed REA launcher or its scripts/rea.mjs file with complete rea-agents package metadata and runtime. Setup help explains where to find it.
wizard.rea.compatibility: REA 6.5.0: eight audited static/read-only tools are available after separate connection and tool approval. Other versions and dynamic/control tools are not verified. Secure Linux resource isolation is checked before REA starts.
wizard.rea.runtime_required: A compatible Node.js installation is required before continuing. See Setup help, then Scan again.
wizard.rea.test_failed: REA could not complete the bounded connection check. Check Linux systemd user isolation, the REA 6.5.0 installation and Setup help. No tools are approved automatically.
wizard.rea.blocked: REA is installed, but secure resource isolation is unavailable on this system. ChromaNeural will not start REA. Local AI and other integrations remain available.
usage.title: External tools - resource Fair Use
usage.optional: External tools are optional. You can continue with local AI without using MCP points. Point consent does not approve additional tools.
usage.loading: Checking resource accounting availability. Local features remain available.
usage.rule: ChromaPoints are consumed according to verified resource use, using the same normalization as contribution earnings. Discovery is free. A tool call is not a fixed point unit.
usage.insufficient: The verified contribution budget cannot cover the bounded resource exposure. The start allowance does not fund MCP. Continue without external tools or cancel.
usage.unavailable: Resource Fair Use is not yet verified: authoritative normalization and trusted resource settlement are unavailable. MCP tool execution is paused; no price or reservation is assumed. Local ChromaNeural features continue normally. Continue without external tools or cancel.
